task.title: Relics: retire and compact relics
task.description:
A relic is a new kind of record in Workbook, separate from tasks. It holds specs, plans, decisions, transcripts and similar material, with the same history and sharing that tasks have. A relic has a title, a type, an author, links, and content made of named parts.

Specs and plans stop being relevant. This story lets someone retire a relic, and lets a project drop the old history of retired and deleted relics by hand.

## Retiring

- `workbook relic retire <relic>` and `unretire`. Both are recorded changes and both can be undone.
- A retired relic keeps its current content and stays readable.
- It leaves default lists (`relic list --retired` shows it) and is shown as retired wherever something links to it.
- If one side of a sync retired a relic and the other edited it, both apply.
- If both sides changed the retired mark, the later sync wins.

## Compaction

Only retired and deleted relics can be compacted. A relic still in use is never compacted. Compaction is always run by hand, with a dry run and a backup bundle written first, as for tasks.

```
workbook compact --relics [--retired-only | --deleted-only]
```

| Boundary | Compacting keeps | Compacting drops |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retired | Current content and links. It stays readable. | Step-by-step history and the text of removed parts |
| Deleted | A stub: title, type, author, dates and links | All content and history |

- The existing `workbook compact` keeps compacting only tasks unless relics are named.
- It works as task compaction does: a parentless checkpoint commit holds the kept state and lists every change it replaces, and the ref moves to it. Publishing that move succeeds only if `origin` still points at the tip that was compacted.
- Links never break. A dropped part or relic leaves a stub, so a link to it says "removed on <date>".
- A deleted relic stays fully recoverable until someone compacts it. After that, the backup bundle is the only copy of its content.
- Restoring a compacted deleted relic brings back the stub and says its content was dropped on that date. Restoring a removed part whose text was dropped is refused with the same explanation.
- An unpublished body edit that started from a dropped version cannot be applied and is reported as a conflict.
- Diffs reach back only to the compaction point.

## Documentation

`AGENTS.md` and the architecture document describe compaction as allowed only on Done and Deleted tasks. Add retired and deleted relics to that rule in both, with the same safeguards.

## Done when

- A retired relic compacts to its current content, and a deleted one to a stub, with a dry run and a bundle first.
- A clone that had not synced before the compaction converges after it.
- Every link into a compacted relic still resolves to a stub or to current content.
- Restore after compaction behaves as described.
- The reference documents retiring and relic compaction.

## Not in this story

Compacting relics that nobody has changed for a while, and compaction that runs by itself. Both were considered and left out.

## Where the design is

The approved design is "Workbook Relics Design" (2026-11-21). It is kept out of the repository. Until "Relics: teach agents to use relics and store the design as the first relic" is done, an untracked copy sits at `specs/2026-11-21-relics-design.html` in Dylan's checkout. After that, read the relic. This description carries what the story needs, and the design wins where the two disagree.
